title: 8th Round of Lebanon-Israel Rome Talks Postponed to October as Diplomatic Calendar Fills Up
detail: September 12, 2026 — The eighth round of US-mediated Lebanon-Israel talks, tentatively set for Rome on September 15-16, has been postponed until October, a US official told Axios. Three overlapping scheduling conflicts were cited: the Jewish high holidays falling in mid-September, a Paris donor conference in support of the Lebanese Armed Forces, and preparations across multiple governments for the UN General Assembly in New York later in the month. Rather than leaving a full gap in the process, Washington is filling the pause with a lower-level stopgap: the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to the US are due to meet in Washington to discuss implementation of the June 26 framework agreement, which covers phased Hezbollah disarmament and an Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon beginning with disputed 'pilot zones.' The postponement compounds the delay flagged September 9, when a Lebanese official said the pilot-zones dispute specifically would not move until after Israel's October elections, splitting the process into separate Rome political and Florida military tracks.
